title: Erasing Error Types via `map_err(|e| e.to_string())`
pattern: Catching a rich, typed error and immediately transforming it into a raw string using `.to_string()`, `format!("{:?}", e)`, or `.map_err(ToString::to_string)`.
why_bad: It erases the structured type metadata of the error. Downstream callers cannot programmatically recover, match on specific failure variants (e.g., `ErrorKind::NotFound`), or retry selective errors without parsing the flat string.
detection: Look for calls to `.map_err()` that invoke `to_string()`, `format!`, or other string conversions where the containing function returns `Result<_, String>`.
counterexample:
Converting an error to a custom structured domain error that wraps the original or maps to a typed enum:
```rust
fn load_config() -> Result<Config, ConfigError> {
    std::fs::read_to_string("config.toml")
        .map_err(ConfigError::IoError)
}
```
source: *Types and Programming Languages* by Benjamin C. Pierce (p. 204, Section 14.1); *Rust for Rustaceans* by Jon Gjengset (p. 137).
